verdict: TransDigm's sales jumped 23% to $2.7B as all three aircraft-parts channels grew by double digits, lifting net income 10% to $540M despite interest costs climbing with its debt-funded deals.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: +22.5% vs a year ago; 13 points of it organic

kpis.label: EBITDA As Defined
kpis.note: 52.8% of sales — the company's preferred profit measure

kpis.label: Share buybacks
kpis.note: repurchased in the quarter; over $1.8B so far in fiscal 2026

segments.name: Power & Control
segments.note: Engines, power systems and other mission-critical aircraft parts — sales rose 32.5% on commercial aftermarket, OEM and defense growth, helped by acquisitions.

segments.name: Airframe
segments.note: Parts for the aircraft body and cabin — sales rose 12.1% across aftermarket, OEM and defense channels.

segments.name: Non-aviation
segments.note: A small business selling similar engineered parts outside aviation — sales rose 15.0% to $46M.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and administrative costs — up 37% as acquired businesses and higher sales added overhead, including acquisition and integration costs.

opex.name: Intangible amortization
opex.note: Non-cash amortization of patents and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions.

takeaways.title: Growth in every channel
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 23% to $2,741M — 13% organic plus acquisitions — with commercial aftermarket up 17% and double-digit growth in commercial OEM and defense as well.

takeaways.title: Margins stay exceptionally high
takeaways.text: EBITDA As Defined was $1,447M, or 52.8 cents of every sales dollar, down slightly from 54.4% only because newly bought businesses carry lower margins at first.

takeaways.title: Interest is the big cost after parts
takeaways.text: Interest expense, net, rose 30% to $514M as borrowings grew to fund deals such as the $2.2B Jet Parts Engineering and Victor Sierra purchase — the price of TransDigm's debt-funded model.

oneTimers: $35M of acquisition transaction and integration-related expenses were added back in the company's adjusted figures (GAAP results include them).
footerNote: Net income of $540M includes $1M attributable to noncontrolling interests; EPS of $9.39 is based on the $539M attributable to TransDigm common stockholders. TransDigm's fiscal year ends September 30 — Q4 FY26 results were not yet reported as of November 7, 2026, so this is the latest reported quarter. Segment sales are from the Form 10-Q for the same period.

sources.label: Quarterly report Form 10-Q — segment sales (SEC EDGAR)
